docs.title: ADR-165: The runbook and the interface name «أثير برايم» / Aether Prime
docs.text:
Date: 2026-11-14 · Status: Proposed. Ahmad's message of 2026-11-14 asked for a runbook page (`#/runbook`) that joins the existing engines with a Node and Python twin, and chose the interface name himself: «أختار أنا بنفسي تغيير اسم الواجهة إلى «أثير برايم» (`Aether Prime`) في النسختين العربية والإنجليزية».
1. **One engine over the engines that exist.** `jarvis/server/lib/runbook.mjs` is pure and is inlined into the page in its own scope. `.claude/skills/replica-runbook/runbook.py` gives the same answers and chain hash (`tests/golden.json`, 19 requests).
2. **Six stages, in order, on one goal and the skills it names:**
   - **shield:** the privacy shield (ADR-158) cleans the goal before anything else reads it. A secret check keeps only the first five hex characters of its SHA-1.
   - **docs:** project search (ADR-164) returns the five best records, reviews and skills for the cleaned goal, with their fused scores, ranks and matching lines.
   - **order:** Kahn's order (ADR-163) of the chosen skills and what they load, from `skill-deps.json`.
   - **tree:** the workbench (ADR-160) on the cleaned goal, read as a behaviour tree (ADR-163). A locked approval keeps it running, and `locked` counts those steps.
   - **plan:** UCB1 (ADR-163) over the three meta-code plans from the person's own record, [INFERENCE].
   - **routes:** one fixed probe per page through the engine behind it: `#/docs`, `#/order`, `#/tree`, `#/polymath`, `#/workbench`, `#/universal`, `#/atlas`, `#/math` and `#/hyper`. Each reports whether the engine gave its checked answer and the first 12 hex characters of the SHA-256 of that answer. `#/diagnostics` reads the running server, so it is listed as `server_only`.
3. **Failures stay local.** A stage whose engine refuses its input is an `error`; the other stages still run and `ready` is false. A SHA-256 chain binds the stages in order.
4. **Facts from the repository only.** Skills, dependencies and documents come from the three snapshots in `jarvis/app/data`

docs.title: ADR-169: Release readiness and the regression gate (#/release)
docs.text:
Date: 2026-11-15 · Status: Proposed. Ahmad's message of 2026-11-15 asked for a deterministic release-readiness check and regression gate, built on main after ADR-168 from the repository's own files, with no assumed numbers and no outside connection. The engine had to be in Node with a Python twin that gives the same answers, and its checks had to be handed to the engines it calls rather than repeated.
1. **One engine in two languages.**
   - `jarvis/server/lib/release-gate.mjs` is pure and is inlined into the page in its own scope.
   - `.claude/skills/replica-release-gate/release_gate.py` uses the standard library, over `replica-skill-tree` and `replica-impact-analysis`.
   - `tests/golden.json` holds 82 requests with the server's answers, 38 of them refusals; Python gives the same answers and chain hashes.
   - The skill tree and impact analysis keep their own input checks. This engine checks only what is its own: the mode, the two snapshots and the list of skills.
2. **`audit`: the repository's traceability.**

docs.title: ADR-170: The architect studio (#/architect)
docs.text:
Date: 2026-11-15 · Status: Proposed. Ahmad's message of 2026-11-15 asked for an architect studio, built on main after ADR-169. It has four parts:
- a domain-separated SHA-256 seal that opens the studio's tools;
- a live scale for text, spacing and numerals;
- a composite skill composer that hands its checks to the engines it calls;
- an upgrade radar.
1. **The route is `#/architect`, not `#/studio`.** `#/studio` is already the Studio of ADR-133 (the preview, the time machine and the exporter). The page is «استوديو المصمم» / Architect studio.

docs.title: replica-architect
headings: In giant-core (these rules override the defaults below)
docs.text:
>-
# replica-architect
`AGENTS.md` and `DESIGN.md` are binding here (ADR-133).
- **Free and open source first.** The default table below names hosted, partly paid services. In this repo, plan free and self-hostable parts first, and mark a paid service as an option Ahmad decides on.
- **Payments are locked.** Anything that moves money, opens trades or takes subscribers is a locked «قيد الموافقة» card until Ahmad approves it separately, with a legal review (AGENTS.md §1). Do not plan Stripe routes as buildable.
- **Same for outward actions.** Deploys to a public domain, outbound messages and repository permission changes are approval items, never automatic.
- **Pages and services.** Pages that must open from `file://` use no framework and no build at runtime, with a strict CSP (`default-src 'none'`, sha256-pinned inline code). Local services bind to `127.0.0.1`. Secrets live in the vault or dotenvx env files, never in code or `localStorage`.
- **Where files go.** Write the plan in the product's own folder (for Jarvis: `jarvis/replica/architecture.md` and `jarvis/replica/schema.sql`), not a repo-root `replica/`.
Reads `replica/recon.md` and `replica/features.csv`. Writes
`replica/architecture.md` (template: architecture.md in this folder).
If there is no recon map, stop and run `/replica-recon` first. Planning a
clone from memory of what an app does is how you miss half of it.
Use what the user already knows if they have a stack. Otherwise the default,
because every part is managed, documented and cheap at zero users:
| layer | default | swap for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| web app | Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript | Remix, SvelteKit, Rails |
| styling | Tailwind, tokens from replica-design | CSS modules |
| mobile | Expo (React Native) | SwiftUI, Kotlin |
| database | Postgres on Supabase or Neon | PlanetScale, SQLite (Turso) |
| ORM | Drizzle or Prisma | raw SQL |
| auth | Supabase Auth or Auth.js | Clerk |
| payments | Stripe Checkout + Billing | Lemon Squeezy, Paddle

docs.title: replica-impact-analysis
docs.text:
Deterministic impact checks over facts the repository already holds - a model name against the 30-family open-weight catalog (its family, what its documented licence allows for personal use or for serving it to others, and the weights' memory from the card's own parameter count and the bits per weight you type), a skill's blast radius (Kahn's layers of what it loads with any cycle named, a reverse breadth-first search of what loads it, the pages and engines to test again, each skill's test command and the matching project documents by BM25 and RRF), and a line-by-line longest-common-subsequence diff of two texts or plans with SHA-256 of each text, the difference and the chain. Nothing is ranked, measured or guessed; running a model stays a locked approval. Standard-library Python only, over the reviewed skills.

docs.title: replica-release-gate
docs.text:
Release readiness over facts the repository already holds - an audit of the skill tree's states (proved, tested, rules, reference, attention) and of the decision records and security reviews in the project-search corpus, ready only when no skill needs attention; a regression gate between two snapshots of the checks' counts that you give (tests passed must not fall, failures, surviving mutants, SkillSpector critical and high, contrast failures and bilingual-purity violations must be 0), with one verdict per check and for the release; and a release bundle that runs impact analysis on the skills a change touched and an optional model, joins the pages and test commands, diffs the release notes line by line and binds the sections with a SHA-256 chain. Publishing stays a locked approval. Standard-library Python only, over the reviewed skills.
# replica-release-gate
```bash
python3 .claude/skills/replica-release-gate/release_gate.py '{"mode": "audit"}' --data jarvis/app/data
python3 .claude/skills/replica-release-gate/release_gate.py '{"mode": "bundle", "skills": ["replica-impact-analysis"], "model": "openai/gpt-oss-120b", "use": "service", "bits": 4}' --data jarvis/app/data
python3 -m unittest discover -s .claude/skills/replica-release-gate/tests
```
- The audit reads only the snapshots in `jarvis/app/data` (`skill-tree-input.json`, `search-corpus.json`). The verdict is `ready` when no skill needs attention, `attention` otherwise, and `empty` with no skill.
- Shares are the proved, tested and proved-or-tested skills over all skills, to four decimals. Missing decision-record numbers are listed as facts, not failures.
- Regression gate:
  - **Counts that should grow** (server, app and live tests passed, mutants killed): `regression` when the candidate is lower, `progress` when higher, `steady` when equal.
  - **Failure counts** (failed tests, surviving mutants, SkillSpector critical and high, contrast failures, purity violations): `regression` when the candidate is above 0,

docs.title: replica-runbook
docs.text:
One goal and the skills it needs, run through the engines this repository already has, in order - the privacy shield cleans the goal (a secret check gives only its SHA-1 prefix), project search finds the matching records and reviews, Kahn's order lays out the chosen skills and what they load, the workbench on the cleaned goal is read as a behaviour tree, UCB1 picks one of the three meta-code plans from the person's own record, and one fixed probe per page checks the engine behind it; a SHA-256 chain binds the stages. Nothing is sent or installed, and every outbound, install or publish step stays a locked approval. Standard-library Python only, over the reviewed skills.
# replica-runbook
```bash
python3 .claude/skills/replica-runbook/runbook.py '{"goal": "Heal the contrast of the login page", "skills": ["replica-polymath-engine"]}' --data jarvis/app/data
python3 -m unittest discover -s .claude/skills/replica-runbook/tests
```
- The goal is cleaned by the privacy shield before any other stage reads it.
- Skills, documents and dependencies come only from the snapshots in `jarvis/app/data` (`skill-tree-input.json`, `skill-deps.json`, `search-corpus.json`). Nothing is fetched.
- A stage whose engine refuses its input is an `error`; the other stages still run, and `ready` is false.
- A locked approval in the workbench keeps the tree `running`; `locked` counts those steps. Nothing here approves them.
- Each page probe runs one fixed input through the engine behind the page. `#/diagnostics` reads the running server, so it is `server_only`.
- The plan choice carries [INFERENCE].
- Same answers and chain hash as `jarvis/server/lib/runbook.mjs`: `tests/golden.json`.
